notes: Single source of truth for the tiered UI gate (see e2e/README-gate.md). Paths are relative to apps/org-ui unless a glob starts with ../ (repo root).
Journeys are the tests tagged @journey in the specs. Each entry names one test declaration (spec + a unique substring of its test( line) and how many Playwright tests it expands to.
A change that matches a category's sources runs that whole category in addition to the journeys. A path that matches nothing and is not ignored runs the full suite (fail closed).
webkit: true marks journeys that are also in the WebKit subset; the flag must equal whether the journey's test( line carries the @webkit tag that the webkit project in playwright.config.ts selects.

webkitExempt lists the files Playwright runs that exercise keyboard or focus (directly or through a local e2e helper) but that the webkit project does not select (a statically skipped test does not count), each with a reason; ui-gate.test.ts (reading Playwright's own --list) fails on such a file that is not listed, and on a stale entry. A @webkit tag counts only where the webkit project selects it. Known limits (README-gate.md): coverage is per file, so one @webkit test covers the whole file (BUG-169c), and a skip decided at run time is not visible to --list.

allowedCoupling.why: Dedicated pointer-focus regressions (BUG-158/166/168): each asserts focus return on the page whose shared primitive or handler is fixed (the org chart View menu, the Offices Retry buttons, the project Remove dialog); the shared primitives are covered by shell-look.

Dedicated ProcessSheet caller-override regression for the shared Button outline. The helper also samples nine consumer families (documented route-scanner limit); shared primitive changes select FULL, page-only changes retain their category and journey coverage.
The layout only calls provideDraftStore (kept shared in messaging/drafts); the barrel is loaded on every page, so an import-time failure in any chat file shows in the always-run journeys.
Every spec creates its organization through /create or /welcome as set-up; the org-lifecycle category and the create/open journeys cover those pages.

These specs open Offices or Chat mainly for shell chrome (topbar, footer, navigation focus, Back), but they also assert page-owned states (for example a stopped office or an offline chat shown inside the shell). Accepted speed tradeoff: a page change does not re-run them; a shared or unknown change does.
